Title: Johor Plantations' palm oil complex opens new growth avenue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Plantations Group Bhd's move into higher-value downstream palm oil products through its Integrated Sustainable Palm Oil Complex (iSPOC) could open a new earnings growth avenue from financial year 2027 (FY27).
Apex Securities Bhd, which has initiated coverage on the company, said the complex would mark Johor Plantations' transition beyond bulk crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel production into value-added palm-based products.
"Successful commissioning and utilisation ramp-up could meaningfully lift earnings from FY27 and potentially support a higher valuation multiple as the earnings mix shifts towards value-added downstream products," it said in a note.
Located in Sedali, Johor, iSPOC is scheduled to be commissioned in the second half of FY26.
A key component of the complex is a specialty fats and oils refinery, which will mark Johor Plantations' entry into the downstream segment and enable the group to produce premium palm-based products.
Apex Securities said upstream and midstream operations remained the group's core businesses, contributing RM1.3 billion and RM457 million respectively, or about 99 per cent of its FY25 revenue.
Meanwhile, the developing El Nino weather phenomenon could support CPO prices as prolonged hot and dry conditions risk reducing palm oil production with a lag.
Apex Securities said the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration sees a greater than 90 per cent probability of a very strong El Nino during the Northern Hemisphere autumn and winter of 2026 and 2027.
"The key catalyst would be downward revisions to Malaysian and Indonesian production expectations as El Nino develops, potentially extending the current high-CPO-price environment into FY27," it said.
Apex Securities said a tighter supply outlook would benefit Johor Plantations given its predominantly upstream earnings exposure.
Higher realised CPO prices could translate into stronger margins as a significant portion of plantation costs would not rise proportionately with selling prices, it added.
Apex Securities has a "Buy" call on Johor Plantations with a target price of RM2.23.

Title: Ex-SD Guthrie supervisor gets RM127,600 after dismissal over sexual harassment claims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Industrial Court has awarded RM127,600 to a former SD Guthrie Bhd field supervisor after ruling that allegations of sexual harassment, threats and insubordination used to justify his dismissal were not proven.
Industrial Court chairman Augustine Anthony criticised the company's disciplinary process, describing some of the charges against E. S. Munusamy as an "afterthought".
Munusamy, who had served SD Guthrie for 34 years, was dismissed on July 11, 2024, following two domestic inquiries into allegations that he had sexually harassed a male worker, threatened to kill him and burn down his house, and disobeyed company instructions in December 2023.
He joined the company as a general worker in 1990 and later rose to become a field supervisor, or mandore, at its Sungai Buloh estate.
The court noted inconsistencies in the complainant's accounts, including the absence of claims in his initial police report that Munusamy had touched his chest and buttocks, torn his shirt and made sexual remarks.
Anthony said the differing accounts raised serious doubts about the reliability of the complainant's version.
The court also rejected allegations that Munusamy later threatened to murder the complainant and burn him or his living quarters.
Anthony questioned why such serious allegations, which allegedly occurred on the same day, were not included in the first show-cause letter or the first domestic inquiry.
"Instead, they surfaced after Munusamy, who had been suspended since December 2023, engaged a lawyer to push for a conclusion to the disciplinary proceedings.
"His lawyer wrote to the company's headquarters on Feb 5, 2024.
"The first domestic inquiry notice was issued on Feb 9, followed by a second show-cause letter on Feb 16 and a second domestic inquiry notice on March 20.
"The timing is a matter of acute curiosity for this court. There was clear afterthought that the company never explained," he said.
Anthony said the circumstances indicated that the later charges had been brought after Munusamy sought outside assistance.
"All the facts of this case point to a retaliatory act on the part of the company against the claimant simply because he wanted a prompt conclusion to all the unproven allegations against him by seeking external help."
The court also dismissed the insubordination allegations, noting that although Munusamy refused to sign acknowledgement of the show-cause letter, he submitted his written explanation within the deadline.
The court made a similar finding over Munusamy's alleged refusal to acknowledge a domestic inquiry notice, noting that he had attended the inquiry as directed.
"The presence of the claimant in the inquiry itself is a reflection that he had respectfully complied with the direction or orders of the company to attend the proceedings.
"This court finds that the company has failed to prove on the balance of probabilities that the dismissal of the claimant from his employment with the company was with just cause or excuse," he said.
The court also raised concerns over Munusamy's remuneration after 34 years of service.
SD Guthrie said his monthly salary was RM1,249.71, while Munusamy claimed he earned RM1,700.
In the absence of sufficient evidence to support the RM1,700 figure, the court fixed his monthly salary at RM1,500.
Anthony said Munusamy's pay after 34 years of service warranted "much introspection and soul searching" within the plantation industry.
The court awarded Munusamy RM52,800 in back wages, equivalent to 24 months, and RM74,800 in compensation in lieu of reinstatement based on his 34 years of service.

Title: Yen weak ahead of BoJ decision, rate hike expected
Article:
SINGAPORE: The yen got off to a weak start against the dollar and the euro at the start of Asian trading on Friday, with currency markets in a subdued mood ahead of an expected rate hike from the Bank of Japan (BoJ) later in the trading session.
The yen fell 0.1 per cent to 156.19 yen per dollar, resuming its decline after snapping a three-day losing streak on Thursday as traders prepare for the Japanese central bank to lift interest rates to the highest level in more than three decades. Against the euro, the yen was 0.2 per cent weaker at 179.3000 yen.
The yen's softness followed data released Friday which showed Japanese inflation fell slightly short of expectations in August. Swaps pricing indicates that the market views a hike from the BoJ as 83 per cent likely, with quarterly rate hikes expected to follow, according to data from LSEG.
"Given the degree of pricing, the rate decision itself may have limited impact on the yen," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone Group in Melbourne. "Instead, attention should fall on the forward swaps curve and the bank's guidance around the pace and urgency of further tightening."
"Governor Ueda's press conference will therefore be key. The market will be looking for confirmation that further normalisation remains firmly on the table, while assessing whether the Bank sees any urgency to move again."
The British pound was flat at a 2-1/2-month low of US$1.3359 after the Bank of England held interest rates on Thursday and unexpectedly paused sales of government bonds for six months.
The euro was flat at US$1.1478. The Aussie dollar was 0.1 per cent firmer at US$0.7117 as Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock warned lawmakers that risks to inflation flagged by policymakers appeared to be materialising. Its kiwi counterpart was down 0.1 per cent at US$0.5724.
The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was flat at 100.2100, after edging back from a 2-1/2-month high on Thursday.
Traders narrowly expect a hike from the Federal Reserve next month as investors say they are becoming more confident in Chair Kevin Warsh's efforts to reassert the central bank's independence from the White House.
Fed funds futures are pricing an implied 53 per cent probability of a quarter-point hike at the central bank's next two-day meeting next month, compared with a 27.2 per cent chance a week ago, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.
Oil prices started the day lower, with Brent crude futures off one per cent at US$103.76 per barrel as traders reassess supply risks after Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis traded strikes on Thursday.
China has asked Tehran to help rein in the Houthis after their military blitz over the past week, three Iranian sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin slid 0.1 per cent to US$76,442.97 while ether was down 0.2 per cent at US$2,447.39.

Title: Oil prices fall 1pct on hopes of limited supply disruptions
Article:
HOUSTON: Oil prices fell about one per cent, extending losses for a third session, but stayed above US$100 on Friday, as hopes of alternative ways for barrels from the Middle East to reach markets outweighed concerns about strikes between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis.
Brent crude futures fell US$1.01, or one per cent, to US$103.77 a barrel by 0020 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate futures fell US$1.03, or one per cent, to US$100.88 a barrel.
Both benchmarks had closed down about one per cent on Thursday.
Markets largely shrugged off concerns about new threats to supplies even as Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis exchanged fresh strikes across their border on Thursday, expanding the Middle East war front.
Oil prices had climbed to around four-month highs this week as sources said crude loadings at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export hub of Yanbu had been suspended and Riyadh had cancelled some deliveries to Europe after its East-West pipeline was damaged in an attack last week.
Sources that have spoken to Reuters have given varying estimates of how long it will take to reopen the pipeline and return crude flows to normal.
Three of the pipeline's pumping stations - one more than assessed previously - were damaged, according to satellite imagery and three industry sources. A prolonged closure of the pipeline to Yanbu could cut off as much as four per cent of global oil supply, traders have said.
Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia was seeking to return about half the capacity of its East-West oil pipeline within days after the critical link to the Red Sea was halted last week following drone attacks.
Saudi Arabia was also offering more crude cargoes to Asian refiners through ship-to-ship transfers off Oman's Sohar port, a move that would help offset some of the disruption caused by attacks on the East-West pipeline.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright has said that crude should be flowing through the pipeline within days.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said a Togo-flagged oil tanker was struck while attempting to make an "illegal passage" through the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, Iranian state media said early on Friday.
Highlighting uncertainty, JPMorgan said on Thursday it does not have a clear baseline view for oil markets for the first time since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The US and Iran have held no peace talks since an interim agreement reached in June collapsed within weeks.
The war will come up for discussion at the United Nations General Assembly next week, and an Iranian delegation will be able to attend, according to the US State Department.

Title: #NSTviral: Sea turtle makes surprise visit behind woman's home
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A woman got an unexpected visitor when a sea turtle came ashore at night and made its way onto the sandy area behind her home.
In a Threads post by
@nvdivsharheera
, she shared several pictures showing the turtle just a few metres from her house.
"Our special guest. It came up right behind the house. See you again," she wrote.
The post caught the attention of social media users, garnering more than 335,000 views and 20,000 likes.
In response to questions, the woman said the turtle was believed to have come ashore at 8pm and spent several hours digging in the sand.
"There were no eggs. It took about three hours just to dig the hole. I did not feel like waiting.
"It came up after 8pm. I only waited until 10pm. It took too long and I did not feel like waiting any longer. I don't know whether it laid any eggs," she said.
A check of the comments showed several users advising her to report the sighting to the Fisheries Department and avoid disturbing the turtle should it return.
One user, @mermaidudu, said turtles could come ashore to assess whether an area was suitable for nesting, adding that digging did not necessarily mean eggs had been laid.
"Turtles may also create a 'false nest' to distract predators," she said.
She urged the woman to inform the Fisheries Department, saying the turtle could return to the same area to nest.
Another user, @qasseuurina_, gave similar advice, saying the turtle might return if it had not laid eggs.
Several users also reminded the public not to disturb nesting turtles with bright lights or camera flashes.
"If it comes ashore again, don't use a direct flash as they are sensitive to light. Keep the area dark if possible," wrote @erinaziz.
Another commenter, @nurulainni65, warned that white lights and camera flashes could affect turtles, including temporarily affecting their vision and causing stress.
User @fatinnmaisara also urged the woman to report the sighting and avoid making loud noises, shining white lights or standing in front of the turtle if it returned.
The woman's home is understood to be very close to the sea. She also claimed that some houses in the area had already been submerged due to changes in the coastline.
As of press time, the exact location of the incident and the turtle species could not be confirmed based on the post.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Girl kicked, pushed by friends after taunting incident in Miri
Article:
MIRI: A girl was kicked and pushed by a group of friends following a dispute sparked by a taunting incident at an open area in Tudan Desaras Phase 6 here.
The incident was captured in a 44-second video, which has since gone viral on Facebook.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said police received a report concerning the video, which showed several boys and girls involved in a fight.
He said the incident occurred around 5pm on Wednesday in front of one of the children's houses.
"Police have identified all seven children involved in the video, aged between eight and 13.
"They are all friends who frequently play together," he said in a statement.
Farhan said preliminary investigations found that the fight broke out after the victim allegedly taunted one of the children using vulgar language, which angered the others.
"The victim was subsequently kicked and pushed by the other children involved. However, the child seen being struck in the video did not suffer any serious injuries," he said.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code.

Title: Service and dedication to fairness: True legacy of judicial leadership
Article:
LETTERS:
I read with deep appreciation the NST report "CJ: Judges' Legacies Make a Judiciary".
I could not agree more with the profound observation by Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh:
"A judiciary is built not merely of marble and mahogany, but on the legacies of our judicial predecessors. It is not built by grand courthouses, but by the character, conduct and legacy of the judges who serve within it."
This is a truth that every Malaysian should cherish. We are rightly proud of the Palace of Justice in Putrajaya, yet no building — however grand — can sustain public trust on its own.
The true strength of our judiciary lies in the judgments handed down, the integrity shown in court, and the independence upheld without fear or favour.
The Chief Justice's tribute to four former leaders of our judiciary — Tun Mohamed Eusoff Chin, Tun Mohamed Dzaiddin Abdullah, Tun Abdul Hamid Mohamad, and Tun Siti Norma Yaakob — reminds us that legacies are made not by titles, but by service.
These men and women understood that justice is not just a matter of power; it is a promise to the people.
They lived by the principle "hakim bukan Parlimen" — judges do not make the law, they uphold it — and in doing so, they strengthened the very foundation of our nation.
Our country's judicial independence is more than an ideal written in the Constitution. It is the foundation of Malaysia's good name in the world.
Foreign investors look to our country not just for infrastructure or resources, but because they trust that agreements will be respected, disputes settled fairly, and the law applied equally to everyone.
We have been blessed with many such outstanding judges over the years. Their work stands as a bright example for all who follow.
The Palace of Justice may stand tall, but it is the people inside who make it truly just.
May that spirit of fairness, integrity, and independence continue to guide us for generations to come.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
KUALA LUMPUR

Title: Hannah Yeoh, A-G arrive at Istana Negara ahead of Pardons Board meeting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar arrived at Istana Negara this morning ahead of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting.
Yeoh's vehicle entered the palace grounds at 7.48am, followed shortly by a vehicle believed to be carrying the A-G.
Both are members of the board, which is chaired by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
The meeting comes amid reports that the board will reconvene today with a single item on the agenda regarding former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon application.
The application was deferred at the 63rd Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting on Sept 11, with consideration postponed to a subsequent meeting.
Under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya comprises the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and not more than three other members appointed by His Majesty.
Last night, Yeoh denied that her signature appeared on a document that went viral concerning Najib's house arrest issue.
No official announcement has been made on the outcome of today's meeting as of this morning.

Title: Johan Setia records highest API reading at 198
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality in several areas across the country remained unhealthy, with Johan Setia in Selangor recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 198 as at 8am today.
Data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed 34 stations recorded unhealthy API readings, while 31 recorded moderate readings and three recorded good readings.
Kuching in Sarawak recorded an API reading of 192, followed by Samarahan at 184.
Nilai in Negri Sembilan recorded 181, followed by IPD Serian in Sarawak at 180 and Seri Manjung in Perak at 176.
Putrajaya recorded 173, while Tasek Ipoh in Perak recorded 172.
Shah Alam and Seremban recorded 171 each, followed by Banting at 167.
Cheras recorded 166, while Alor Gajah in Melaka recorded 165.
Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 164, followed by Petaling Jaya and Bukit Rambai in Melaka at 162 each.
Klang recorded 161, while Port Dickson and Tangkak in Johor recorded 159 each.
Segamat in Johor and Sibu in Sarawak recorded 158 each, followed by Sarikei in Sarawak at 157.
Batu Pahat recorded 155, while Bandaraya Melaka, Bintulu and Sri Aman recorded 153 each.
Pengkalan Pegoh in Ipoh and Tanjung Malim in Perak recorded 152 each, as did Kluang in Johor.
Temerloh in Pahang recorded 151, followed by Kuala Selangor at 148.
Larkin in Johor recorded 128, while Jerantut recorded 107.
Mukah in Sarawak recorded the lowest API reading among the stations listed, at 104.
Under the API classification, readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.

Title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar as oil prices ease
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and a basket of major currencies on Friday, supported by improved market sentiment as easing Middle East crude oil supply concerns lifted risk appetite.
At 8am, the local note increased to 4.0955/1015 against the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0965/1010.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market sentiment was lifted after Saudi Arabia reportedly began restoring its damaged East-West pipeline, while tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz continued, easing immediate concerns over supply.
"As a result, Brent crude oil prices fell 0.95 per cent to US$104.82 per barrel, while US Treasury yields declined, with the two- and 10-year notes falling seven basis points each to 4.67 per cent and 4.94 per cent, respectively.
"However, attention has now shifted to the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) monetary policy decision later today, with consensus expecting a 25-basis-point increase in its policy rate to 1.25 per cent," he told Bernama.
He said the market would be closely watching the BoJ's economic assessment and policy tone, as a more hawkish stance could trigger further unwinding of yen carry trades and heighten volatility in the foreign exchange market.
Hence, Mohd Afzanizam expects the ringgit to stay in a narrow range today as traders will be observing this critical event.
At the opening, the ringgit was higher against a basket of major currencies.
The local note gained against the euro to 4.7000/7069 from Thursday's close of 4.7003/7055, rose against the yen to 2.6228/6268 from 2.6305/6336, and advanced vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.4704/4784 from 5.4877/4937 previously.
The ringgit traded mixed against its Asean peers.
The local currency appreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.2096/2146 from 3.2099/2137, but dipped against the Thai baht to 12.3043/3279 from 12.2734/2917.
The ringgit remained unchanged vis-à-vis the Philippine peso at 6.53/6.54 and against the Indonesian rupiah at 230.7/231.1 yesterday.

Title: University student to be charged over Kluang crash that killed four
Article:
KLUANG: A 19-year-old university student is expected to be charged at the magistrate's court this morning over a reckless driving incident that claimed the lives of four family members in June.
The suspect will face charges before magistrate Nurasidah A Rahman under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for driving recklessly and dangerously along Jalan Renggam-Simpang Renggam.
Under Section 42(1), an offender faces a maximum jail sentence of five years, a fine between RM5,000 and RM15,000, and disqualification from holding or obtaining a driving licence for at least two years upon conviction.
It is understood that the charge was framed after the investigation paper was completed by the Johor legal adviser's office and submitted to the prosecution for further action.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh had previously said the investigation paper concerning the suspect had been referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers.
On June 1, four family members were killed while two others were injured in a five-vehicle crash around  1.15pm in front of the Simpang Renggam prison.
The crash involved a Perodua Alza, Proton Wira, Mercedes-Benz, BMW, and Toyota Vios.
The deceased, who were all travelling in the Toyota Vios, were identified as Aiman Mohd Rashid, 36, Nor Azlina Abd Latip, 33, Semek Mat Soh, 73, and 10-year-old Nur Airish Syifa Sidek.
The
accident was suspected to have been caused by the suspect
, who was driving a Mercedes-Benz A250, and his 22-year-old brother, who was behind the wheel of a BMW 530, both allegedly speeding and driving recklessly.
However, the suspect's brother died while being taken to a private hospital for treatment.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar previously directed police to classify the
investigation into the fatal crash as murder
.
However, he said a final decision on the charges would only be determined after the AGC thoroughly examined the results of the police probe.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korea to extend fuel tax cut through November amid price burdens
Article:
SEOUL: South Korea will extend its fuel tax cut scheme by another two months through November to ease price burdens on the public amid protracted tensions in West Asia, the Finance Ministry said Friday.
Yonhap reported the finance and economy minister said the decision was made during an economy-related ministers' meeting chaired by finance minister Koo Yun-cheol, citing the need to ease the public's burden from fuel costs.
Under the measure, the current tax reductions of 15 per cent for gasoline and 25 per cent for diesel and butane, originally set to expire at the end of this month, will remain in place through the end of November.
"We have decided to maintain the current tax cut scheme, considering the country's capacity to address a possible increase in oil price volatility," the finance ministry said in a release.
The country has decided to maintain larger tax cuts for diesel, which is essential for industrial and logistics activities, and butane, which is widely used as fuel for small trucks, it added.

Title: Australia's central bank chief warns inflation risks appear to be materialising
Article:
SYDNEY: Australia's top central banker said on Friday some of the upside risks to inflation flagged by policymakers appeared to be materialising, with the Middle East conflict and the artificial intelligence boom putting upward pressure on prices.
Appearing before lawmakers, Michele Bullock, governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), said a key question facing policymakers at its policy meeting this month would be whether three rate hikes this year would be sufficient to bring inflation back to target in a reasonable time.
The RBA held interest rates steady at 4.35 per cent for a second meeting in August, but it singled out the Middle East war and a global data centre investment boom as key risks to inflation. Both have since moved in an inflationary direction.
"Developments since then suggest that although growth in the Australian economy is slowing, some of these upside risks to inflation appear to be materialising," said Bullock.
She added the economy was slowing down as expected, but the labour market remains tight, warning a period of subdued growth in aggregate demand is needed to bring inflation down.
Markets imply a 93 per cent chance the RBA will lift rates for a fourth time this year to 4.6 per cent when it meets on Sept 28 to 29, and reach 4.85 per cent by early 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran strikes, detains oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Friday they struck an oil tanker sailing under the Togolese flag in the Strait of Hormuz, state news agency IRNA reported.
Teheran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait since the United States and Israel struck Iran in late February.
The Islamic republic wants to charge tolls for passage, attacking ships it accuses of attempting to circumvent its preferred route.
"The Togo-flagged oil tanker 'Trend' had been targeted and detained after a fire broke out on board," the statement said, referring to an attempted "illegal passage" through the vital waterway.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) announced Thursday a "security incident in the Strait of Hormuz, 16 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman."
UKMTO did not provide details about the vessel involved, and it is unclear whether it is the same mentioned by the Revolutionary Guards.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bank of Japan set to raise interest rates to 31-year high
Article:
TOKYO: The Bank of Japan (BoJ) is set to raise interest rates to a 31-year high on Friday and pledge to deliver more to counter inflation risks, which may heighten if the start of a US rate-hike cycle weakens the yen against the dollar.
The widely expected move would be the first hike in three months and take interest rates closer to levels the BoJ deems neutral to the economy, marking another step away from decades of ultra-low rates that cemented the yen's status as a cheap global funding currency.
But the Federal Reserve's rate hike on Wednesday and prospects of another move later this year have piled pressure on the BoJ to keep pace, as a widening of an already big US-Japan rate gap could weaken the yen and lift inflation through higher import costs, analysts say.
Such pressure could affect the tone of BoJ governor Kazuo Ueda's post-meeting briefing, which will be closely watched by markets for clues on the timing and pace of further increases.
"If the Fed were to raise rates again in December, the BoJ could be forced to do so too," said Mari Iwashita, executive rates strategist at Nomura Securities. "It's looking increasingly like a global rate-hike competition."
At the two-day meeting ending on Friday, the BoJ is set to raise its policy rate to 1.25 per cent from one per cent. Board member Toichiro Asada, who dissented to the rate hike in June, may do so again, analysts say.
A hike to 1.25 per cent would bring the BoJ's policy rate to levels unseen since 1995. It would also bring the rate within its estimated 1.1 per cent to 2.5 per cent range of Japan's nominal neutral rate, or the level that neither cools nor overheats growth, thus raising questions about how far it could eventually hike rates.
The BoJ exited a decade-long stimulus in 2024 and raised rates several times, including in June, at a pace of roughly twice a year on the view Japan was making progress in durably achieving its two per cent inflation target.
Critics say the slow pace of BoJ hikes has been among factors keeping the yen weak which, along with surging energy costs from the Iran war, have led to a spike in wholesale inflation that is seen spilling over to consumer prices.
AMBIGUITY MAY PREVAIL
Core consumer inflation held steady near the BoJ's two per cent target in August, data showed on Friday, as companies continued to pass on rising costs for a wide range of food and grocery items.
Even with Friday's expected hike, the BoJ still lags global peers with its policy rate lower than that of the European Central Bank, which raised its key rate last week to 2.5 per cent, and the Fed's 3.75 per cent to four per cent range.
Markets have nearly fully priced in September rate hike after a slew of hawkish BoJ signals, including its warning in July of the risk of an inflation overshoot from soaring fuel costs, rising import costs from a weak yen and strong AI demand.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also piled in, saying he voiced his strong support for "decisive" monetary steps to combat yen weakness in a meeting with Ueda this month, held on the sidelines of a G20 finance leaders' gathering.
But many BoJ officials, including Ueda, have remained vague on the potential speed and degree of future rate hikes, arguing that much would depend on the inflation outlook and how the bank's past rate hikes could affect financial conditions.
"Given deepening uncertainty over the Middle East conflict, the BoJ probably wants to leave itself as much free hand as it can on policy," said Tetsuya Inoue, executive economist at Sony Financial Group. "I doubt governor Ueda will say anything clear-cut on the neutral or terminal rate."
Analysts polled by Reuters expect the BoJ to hike rates to 1.25 per cent on Friday, 1.5 per cent by end-March next year and then to 1.75 per cent in the second quarter of 2027. Most saw the terminal rate as being at least 1.75 per cent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Journalists' Syndicate: Sick and injured journalists in Gaza face harsh conditions and need medical evacuation
Article:
RAMALLAH: The Palestinian Journalists' Syndicate said that journalists and media workers in the Gaza Strip are facing exceptional and harsh conditions amid the ongoing genocidal war carried out by Israeli occupation forces.
The Syndicate said that journalists and media workers in the Gaza Strip are working in an extremely dangerous environment amid shelling and displacement, deteriorating humanitarian conditions, the collapse of large parts of the healthcare system, and shortages of medicines and medical supplies.
According to Palestinian news agency (WAFA), the syndicate, in a statement issued on Thursday,  said that the suffering of journalists is not limited to the risks of being killed or injured while carrying out their work, but also extends to dozens of cases of serious injuries and illnesses requiring surgeries and specialised medical care that is not sufficiently available inside the Strip, noting that 40 journalists in the Strip need medical evacuation and treatment abroad.
It stressed that the issue of sick and injured journalists whose conditions require urgent medical evacuation outside the Gaza Strip has become an urgent humanitarian and human rights issue, particularly in cases involving serious neurological injuries, limb injuries, chronic illnesses, or requiring specialised surgery and rehabilitation.
The syndicate affirmed that continued delays in treatment or denial of access to appropriate medical care could lead to deterioration in the health conditions of the affected journalists and further endanger their lives. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian bonds, ringgit face fresh Fed & BoJ rate headwinds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's ringgit and bond market may come under renewed pressure if the US Federal Reserve resumes monetary tightening.
This could fuel capital outflows and complicate Bank Negara Malaysia's interest-rate policy, economists said.
The Fed's 25-basis-point hike on Wednesday - its first in more than three years - has heightened market focus on the scope for further tightening and its potential impact on emerging markets including Malaysia.
The move comes as the Fed seeks to contain persistent inflation, including price pressures stemming from elevated crude oil prices amid the US-Iran conflict.
IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said the decision's significance extended beyond the rate increase itself.
Tighter US monetary policy could raise funding costs and global market volatility, he added.
"Companies with unhedged US dollar liabilities could also face higher repayment costs in ringgit terms if the US dollar strengthens, while tighter global financial conditions could increase borrowing costs and volatility across equity and bond markets," he told Business Times.
At the broader macroeconomic level, however, Sedek said Malaysia's domestic demand, export capacity and relatively contained inflation provided some buffer against external monetary tightening.
For the ringgit, he said the prospect of further US rate hikes could create short-term depreciation pressure through changes in interest rate differentials, US dollar demand and global risk sentiment.
However, he viewed the pressure as temporary and maintained his forecast for the ringgit to reach RM4.05 against the US dollar by year-end.
Sedek said the ringgit will ultimately be driven by Malaysia's economic fundamentals, exports, commodity prices, the current account and the broader US dollar cycle.
He said some capital could be temporarily reallocated towards US assets following the recent sell-off and repricing of US Treasury yields, but he did not view this as a permanent withdrawal of foreign capital from Malaysia.
Sedek said the Fed's decision did not automatically require Bank Negara to raise its overnight policy rate (OPR).
The central bank will consider domestic inflation, economic activity, employment, financial conditions, credit growth and external developments.
He maintained that Bank Negara would keep the OPR at 2.75 per cent for the remainder of 2026.
He also did not expect another US hike for the rest of the year although he acknowledged that the Fed's projections indicate one further increase remains possible.
Pressure From Twin Rate Risks
SPI Asset Management managing director Stephen Innes said Malaysia could face greater pressure on its bond market and ringgit if the Fed continues to tighten, particularly as the Bank of Japan (BoJ) also normalises monetary policy.
He said Malaysian government bonds were already under pressure, while the yield premium over Japanese government bonds had fallen sharply as the BoJ tightened.
"Malaysia is effectively being squeezed from both sides. US yields are high, Japanese yields are rising, and the relative appeal of Malaysian duration is shrinking," he said.
This could increase the risk of foreign bond outflows and repatriation, particularly among Japanese investors, Innes said.
He said Bank Negara was not automatically forced to raise rates simply to defend the ringgit or bond market, but the cost of keeping policy unchanged was rising.
"If bond outflows accelerate, the ringgit comes under sustained pressure, and that begins feeding imported inflation, then the hurdle for a Bank Negara hike becomes considerably lower," he said.
Innes agreed with market pricing for a Bank Negara hike in the first quarter of 2027, although this could be brought forward depending on how aggressively the BOJ tightens.
If the Fed delivers another rate hike later this year, he said it would widen the policy rate differential, keep US yields attractive and potentially make foreign investors more selective about holding Malaysian bonds.
Another hike could also eventually weigh on Malaysia's external demand if tighter US financial conditions slow consumption and investment, although the country's domestic growth would provide some offset.
Innes said another Fed hike, particularly if accompanied by continued weakness in Malaysian bonds and persistent ringgit pressure, would make a Bank Negara hike a more immediate possibility.
Even if Bank Negara did not raise rates immediately, markets could increasingly price a higher-for-longer domestic rate structure, he said.
Innes said the significance of the latest Fed move was less about the 25 basis point increase itself and more about its implications for further tightening.
"Oil is obviously a major part of the inflation shock, and central banks normally try to look through the first round impact of an energy spike," he said.
"But the Fed is signalling that it is not prepared to look through it if higher energy costs start leaking into inflation expectations, wages and broader prices."
He said the shift in expectations could keep upward pressure on short-term US yields and maintain a firm US dollar backdrop.
Innes added that continued normalisation by the BOJ could contribute to a broader global hawkish repricing, adding to pressure on Malaysian bonds.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's India trade review must tackle structural barriers: Economists
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's review of its trade framework with India should focus on removing structural barriers and helping Malaysian companies gain greater access to its market, economists said.
The review should broaden the framework's scope beyond goods to address non-tariff barriers and emerging sectors, they added.
Universiti Teknologi Mara senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said the review was timely given the existing trade imbalance and the need to ensure bilateral trade delivered broader benefits for both economies.
"The focus, however, should not simply be on narrowing the deficit as trade balances can also reflect differences in production structures, investment and supply chains," he told Business Times.
Idham said the review should identify why Malaysian companies may not be fully capturing opportunities in the Indian market and address the structural barriers that limit their participation.
"A more diversified export base, stronger business-to-business linkages and greater integration into India's expanding value chains would help make bilateral trade more balanced and sustainable over the longer term," he said.
His comments followed Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani's statement that Malaysia and India were set to review their trade framework over the next three to six months.
Johari said India had stressed the importance of a more balanced trading relationship, noting that Malaysia currently recorded a sizeable trade surplus with India.
In 2025, Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of RM25.37 billion with India, with total bilateral trade reaching RM79.33 billion, down five per cent from RM83.5 billion in 2024.
Malaysia's exports to India rose 0.4 per cent to RM52.35 billion last year, while imports fell 14 per cent to RM26.98 billion.
Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Dr Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said the review of the Malaysia-India Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (MICECA) was apt given changes in the countries' trade and investment landscape since the deal was signed in 2011.
Aimi said the agreement needed to evolve beyond its traditional focus on goods to address non-tariff barriers, rules of origin and emerging areas such as digital trade, semiconductors, fintech and renewable energy.
"The 2011 agreement is goods-heavy. A 2026 review must be services and value-chain heavy," he added.
Idham said the review should look closely at tariff lines where Malaysian products still faced relatively high duties. This is alongside rules of origin, customs procedures and non-tariff measures such as product standards, certification and licensing requirements.
He also said there was scope to strengthen provisions covering services, digital trade and investment, while improving trade facilitation through greater use of digital customs and regulatory cooperation.
"The objective should be to make the agreement more responsive to today's business environment and reduce the practical cost of entering the Indian market," he said.
Aimi similarly highlighted rules of origin and non-tariff barriers as key areas for review, particularly for Malaysia's electrical and electronics and semiconductor industries.
"Current AITIGA uses uniform 35 per cent local value addition. This hurts electronics and semiconductors where value addition is low but supply chains are global.
"India and Malaysia are already discussing Product Specific Rules (PSR) to give flexibility. This is critical for Malaysia's E&E exports," he said.
On sectors with potential for greater Malaysian participation in India, Idham said Malaysia already possessed established industrial and technological capabilities in certain sectors.
They include electrical and electronics, semiconductors and related components, chemicals, palm oil and downstream palm-based products, processed food and halal products.
"There is also potential in healthcare, digital services, renewable energy and other green technologies as India's economy continues to expand," he said.
He said Malaysian companies should pursue higher-value segments and strengthen their distribution networks, partnerships and joint ventures in India rather than focusing solely on increasing export volumes.
"This would allow Malaysian companies to build a more durable presence in one of the world's largest consumer and industrial markets," he said.
Meanwhile, Aimi said Malaysia should likewise use India's vast consumer market to expand trade in both directions.
"Given India's 1.4 billion consumer market, Malaysia should not compete on low-cost mass manufacturing, but on 3 layers," he said.
Aimi identified palm oil and oleochemicals, E&E and machinery as areas where Malaysia could strengthen existing trade, while also expanding into halal products, chemicals, green energy, medical devices and high-value agri-food.
He also pointed to services including healthcare, education, fintech, Islamic finance, construction and engineering as areas where Malaysia was under-exported.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KKIA runway reopens after rectification works
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Flight operations at Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) can resume after the airport's runway was reopened at 11.30pm yeserday following final safety checks, Malaysia Airports said.
In an update on its official Facebook page, Malaysia Airports said flight operations could resume following the reopening.
Malaysia Airports also advised passengers travelling to and from KKIA to check with their respective airlines for the latest flight status updates.
The runway had been temporarily closed since 2.45pm to facilitate rectification works, affecting at least 20 arrival and departure flights.
Checks by Bernama at the airport earlier found that several flights were delayed or cancelled, while several incoming services were diverted to Labuan and Sandakan.
The disruption left some passengers waiting for several hours for updates, with many repeatedly checking flight information displays and airline notifications for revised departure and arrival times.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: France arrests far-right policeman suspected of terrorist plot
Article:
PARIS: A policeman who follows "a violent radical far-right ideology" has been arrested in France on suspicion of plotting a terrorist attack, sources told AFP late on Thursday.
Confirming a report by the TF1/LCI broadcaster, a judicial source said that the man was also suspected of having manufactured weapons, among other crimes.
A separate source close to the case told AFP that the police officer, aged 35, was "apprehended on the street" on August 23.
He has since been placed in detention while awaiting trial.
According to TF1/LCI, the officer "is suspected of having planned to carry out violent attacks against the interests of the state" and of having "manufactured 3D-printed weapons", among other things.
The policeman faces charges including preparing a terrorist act, the unauthorised manufacture or trade in weapons in connection with a terrorist organisation and unauthorised weapon possession.
He is also charged with incitement to terrorism through social media.
The police officer's lawyers had not responded to AFP as of Thursday evening.
The news comes in the wake of revelations that France's far-right National Rally (RN) party expelled another policeman after body cam footage of him making racist comments sparked outrage.
The RN's Marine Le Pen hopes to become France's president in next year's elections after years of seeking to make the anti-immigration party she inherited from her father more palatable to the wider public.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 5 reports lodged over kicking of incense pot
Article:
BERA: Five police reports have been lodged by Orang Asli villagers following a viral incident involving an enforcement team member who allegedly kicked a burning incense pot at Kampung Pathir here on Sept 15.
The incident occurred during a joint enforcement operation at the Tasek Bera Conservation Forest Reserve (Ramsar) site.
District police chief Superintendent Zulkiflee Nazir said the reports were lodged by Orang Asli villagers living near the Tasek Bera between Sept 15 and Wednesday.
"The Orang Asli lodged reports claiming that an individual who was part of the enforcement operation had kicked a sacred object belonging to the community.
"We will record statements from the five complainants, the individual involved and other enforcement team members who were present during the incident," he said when contacted yesterday.
Zulkiflee said the case was being investigated under Section 295 of the Penal Code for defiling a sacred object, which carries a maximum two-year jail sentence.
In the video, an individual is seen kicking the burning incense pot, which had been left in the middle of the road, towards the roadside. The action sparked anger among members of the Orang Asli community who were present at the site.
The villagers claimed that the burning incense pot, known as a
tengkarang
,
was used by the community to offer prayers and perform certain rituals.
The community shared a video of the incident on social media saying that the pot was part of their beliefs and heritage, and that such an action could not be tolerated.
It is learnt that members of the enforcement team had earlier asked the villagers to remove the pot, but they refused. This prompted an officer to push it away with his leg while the pot was still burning.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang govt ready to help Tasek Bera Orang Asli, but needs details [WATCH]
Article:
KUANTAN: The Pahang government is prepared to assist Orang Asli living near Tasek Bera, but delays in providing a list of residents in the settlements have hampered efforts to help them.
Pahang Islamic Religious Affairs, Rural Development and Orang Asli Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Syed Ahmad said there were more than seven villages near the lake, but only one had submitted the required list.
He said during a visit to several Orang Asli settlements near the lake on Aug 3, that he had assured the villagers that the state government wanted to help them continue earning a livelihood.
"I told the Orang Asli families living and earning a livelihood within the Tasek Bera  forest  reserve to provide a list of residents and details of their smallholdings before we can negotiate on their behalf.
"So far, only villagers from Kampung Lubuk Tihang have provided the details to the Orang Asli Development Department (Jakoa). The other villagers have yet to submit the requested information, and they can still do so.
"Jakoa has gone to the villages three times to request the list," he told the
New Straits Times
.
The
NST
reported that some 7,000 Orang Asli villagers living near the lake are seeking negotiations with the authorities after receiving notices in June ordering them to vacate parts of the forest reserve. They were alleged to have encroached into the Tasek Bera Conservation Forest Reserve.
After receiving the notices, the villagers set up guard posts at all village entrances and smallholdings around Tasek Bera to prevent outsiders, including enforcement personnel, from entering. This led to the arrest of five villagers on Sept 15.
Meanwhile, Syed Ibrahim said the list was vital for Jakoa to obtain details of those living in the area, including the locations and sizes of their homes and farms, as well as the number of family members, so that their applications could be assessed.
He said the information would enable the state government to identify genuine residents and determine how it could assist them, including through discussions on the land.
"When I say we (the Pahang government) want to help, it means we will go and negotiate on their behalf. We  are ready to assist those affected.
"We understand that the villagers have been occupying land located within a forest reserve and Ramsar site, but they cannot claim to be the landowners simply because they have been living there for a long time," he said.
Syed Ibrahim said the list of names and locations would also allow the authorities to determine which sections of the land could potentially be gazetted for the villagers.
"We have a system. We do not want the villagers to continue living scattered throughout the forest reserve without proper documentation," he said.
When asked about the delay in submitting the names, Syed Ibrahim expressed concern that outsiders might be taking advantage of the situation by occupying land illegally or manipulating the Orang Asli community.
"Initially, the villagers agreed to submit the information but later did not cooperate. It is difficult to understand why they would not want to provide their names... there might be someone influencing them," he said.
The
NST
has reached out to Kampung Pathir Tok Batin Amir Noor Tan for comment
.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NYT alleges Microsoft, OpenAI knew using news content was theft
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: OpenAI committed "an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions" when it used millions of news articles to train its artificial intelligence models, the New York Times alleged in a court document unsealed on Thursday.
The San Francisco-based artificial intelligence lab scraped content from more than 10 million articles, nearly a third of which came from the New York Times alone.
The document claims Microsoft's Director of Applied Science Brent Hect called it "an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions" and possibly the "largest theft of labour in human history."
Hect also allegedly warned that OpenAI might have engaged in an "accidental cover up" in its attempts to identify content in its systems that came from the New York Times and the lawsuit's other plaintiffs.
The newspaper sued OpenAI and Microsoft three years ago in New York federal court for allegedly stealing its copyrighted material to train OpenAI's flagship model, ChatGPT. Microsoft first invested in OpenAI in 2019.
Several other news publishers also joined the lawsuit, including Ziff Davis – which owns CNET and other tech news publications – as well as the parent company of the magazine Mother Jones, the investigative news site The Intercept, and multiple local newspapers across the United States.
They are seeking damages for each article that was allegedly stolen and used by OpenAI's models, though it is unclear what the total amount of penalties could reach.
OpenAI has signed content licensing deals with many news publishers around the world since it launched ChatGPT in late 2022, but concerns persist that generative AI software is reducing traffic to internet news sites.
AI companies have tried to alleviate those concerns by adding citations with links to user queries, but the effort has been criticized as insufficient.
"No matter how prominently we show the links, users won't click," one of OpenAI's own engineers admitted, according to the court document.
Microsoft and OpenAI argue that their use of news content is transformative and falls under "fair use" laws.
In early September, the US Department of Justice filed a brief in support of OpenAI and Microsoft, in which it invoked "scientific progress," economic growth, and "national security."
The plaintiffs have requested a summary judgement in their favour.
If granted by US District Judge Sidney Stein, the case would not go to trial, but a ruling is not expected until 2027.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: N.Korea leader's sister blasts US drills, threatens 'more offensive' response
Article:
SEOUL: The powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un accused the United States of escalating regional tensions through frequent military drills and warned of a "more offensive" response from Pyongyang, according to a statement published by state media Friday.
"The present situation, in which new records are set in terms of practical action hostile toward the DPRK, stresses the need to break records in our responsive action, proportional or more offensive in its nature," the KCNA news agency quoted Kim Yo Jong as saying, using North Korea's official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.
Referring to joint military drills held in recent months by US forces and allies in the Asia-Pacific region as a "US-led war rehearsal," Kim vowed that "our will to defend our sovereignty will be expressed in clearer action and there will be never ever change in the course of intensifying the nuclear war deterrence."
"I remind the enemy once again that if it is judged that the supreme interests of our nation and its military sovereignty and security environment in the region have been seriously violated by their military maneuovers," Kim went on, North Korea's military will "mobilise all means available to cope with it."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US F-16 warplane crashes in Michigan
Article:
WASHINGTON: A Texas-based US military F-16 fighter jet crashed Thursday during a training mission in Michigan, with the pilot able to eject, the unit to which the aircraft belonged said.
"A Texas Air National Guard F-16 Fighting Falcon assigned to the 149th Fighter Wing...crashed during a routine training mission" near Traverse City, the unit said in a statement on its Facebook page.
"The pilot successfully ejected from the aircraft. The incident is under investigation," it added, without providing further details.
Grand Traverse County Emergency Management in Michigan said on Facebook that an evacuation order is "in effect due to a plane crash."
And Gary Peters, one of the northern state's two US senators, said on X that he was "aware of the plane crash near Traverse City" and was "closely monitoring the situation as we work to get more information on the incident."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Takaichi keeps key ministers
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi yesterday retained key ministers in a cabinet reshuffle that seeks to shore up political support to push through her flagship spending plans amid jittery financial markets.
In her first reshuffle since taking office last October, Takaichi kept Satsuki Katayama as finance minister, a move that provides continuity in Japan's exchange-rate policy.
Katayama played a key role negotiating with United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on a rare joint US-Japan yen intervention in late July, an effort that underscored the countries' close cooperation.
However, in a sign that she has no intention of reining in her big spending plans, Takaichi also kept her reflationist ally Minoru Kiuchi as economy minister.
Other key ministers, including some of her competitors in last year's race to lead the ruling party, such as Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, saw no change in their posts.
Takachi also appointed Hiroshi Nakatsuka from the Japan Innovation Party as minister in charge of deregulation.
The new line-up was announced by Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara, who also retained his post.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia to begin e-commerce tax collection
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
JAKARTA: Indonesia will begin making e-commerce platforms collect income taxes from sellers starting Oct 1, a month earlier than previously announced, local media reported yesterday, citing the tax chief.
The move reverses a delay ordered by the previous finance minister and follows a shake-up at the top of the Finance Ministry this week.
The ministry and the tax office did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Some of the biggest platforms operating in Southeast Asia's largest economy were originally tasked by the tax office to start collecting taxes from sellers beginning in August, but then-finance minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa ordered a delay on Aug 5 because of concern it might hurt purchasing power.
The next day, the tax office said the policy would be delayed to Nov 1 and promised taxes that were already paid would be refunded.
Purbaya was sacked this week and his deputy, technocrat Suahasil Nazara, was named as President Prabowo Subianto's third finance minister in less than two years.
"We will immediately activate the regulation and implementation. They are ready, we are ready," Indonesian Finance Ministry's Tax Department head, Bimo Wijayanto, said, according to CNBC Indonesia, adding that the collection would begin Oct 1.
"There's no drama."
Sources said Purbaya had clashed with top officials in his ministry prior to his removal, including with Bimo, over the reshuffling of hundreds of officials at the ministry.
​Tokopedia, controlled by ByteDance's TikTok and ​partly owned by Indonesia's biggest tech company GoTo, together with Sea Ltd's Shopee, the Alibaba-backed Lazada, and Blibli, had previously been appointed as tax collectors.
Indonesia has a booming e-commerce industry, with an estimated gross merchandise value of US$71 billion in 2025 that is expected to grow to US$140 billion by 2030, according to a report by Google, Singapore state investor Temasek and consultancy Bain & Co.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mada sounds warning as Kedah dam levels fall to 35pc
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Water levels at three irrigation dams have dropped to an average of 35.76 per cent, posing a major challenge to padi farmers ahead of the second planting season.
The Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) said yesterday water levels at the Pedu Dam, Ahning Dam and Muda Dam were at 36.99 per cent, 44.33 per cent and 11.88 per cent, respectively.
It added that the limited reserves meant that irrigation for the upcoming planting season would have to depend on rainfall.
"This situation is expected to become more challenging as projections by the Malaysian Meteorological Department show the probability of an El Nino phenomenon rising to 96 per cent towards the end of the year.
"This has the potential to develop into a stronger phase, bringing hot and dry weather and increasing the risk of rainfall deficits.
"These conditions are expected to pose a challenge to water availability and padi cultivation in the Muda area," it said.
Meanwhile, the Mada Water Supply and Padi Cultivation Committee has set Sept 23 as the start of the second planting season.
Phase One of the sowing period is from Sept 23 to Nov 4, followed by Phase Two (Oct 3 to Nov 14) and Phase Three (Oct 13 to Nov 24).
"For the first planting season, crop grown in 100,641ha of fields are in the final flowering and harvesting stages.
"Up to Sept 16, pre-saturation progress had reached 100 per cent, land preparation at 99 per cent and planting at 98.4 per cent, whereas the harvest rate stood at 9.3 per cent," it said.
Mada called on farmers to use water prudently, adding that it would support irrigation needs in affected areas by maximising drain water recycling and deploying mobile pumps on site.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tok Saimah's secret to longevity is healthy diet
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
At 102, Saimah Sajiman has no complicated formula for staying healthy.
She simply sticks to the routines she has followed for decades, including eating simple food and keeping regular mealtimes.
Fondly known as Tok Saimah, the centenarian from Kampung Rahmat, Sri Lalang, believes that maintaining a healthy diet, particularly choosing boiled food over fried or oily dishes, is among the practices that have helped her stay healthy.
"It is not that I do not eat fried food, but I prefer boiled food such as 'sayur bening' (clear vegetable soup), 'ikan pais' (steamed fish with spices) and traditional village 'ulam' (vegetable salads)," she said at her home.
Born in 1924, Tok Saimah, who has more than 20 grandchildren and 50 great-grandchildren, said she would have her breakfast, lunch and dinner at almost the same time every day.
"For breakfast, I will have something light to line the stomach, usually between 8am and 9am. Lunch is before the zohor prayer and dinner is before the isyak prayer," she said.
Her daughter, Fatimah Surip, 78, said she was grateful that her mother remained in good health and was able to stand while performing her prayers.
"My mother does not suffer from any chronic diseases, just a slight hearing problem. If you want to converse, you have to speak a little louder. She also prefers using a wheelchair to move from one place to another," she said.
Tok Saimah recently gained attention on social media after receiving a visit from Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, last Sunday.
Fatimah said her mother's age and experiences of living through several eras, including the Japanese occupation, British colonial rule and the communist terrorist threat, were among the topics that drew Her Majesty's attention during the visit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 3.7-magnitude quake detected 88km north of Sandakan
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A weak earthquake measuring 3.7 on the Richter scale was detected about 88km north of Sandakan, Sabah, at 10.30pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement on Facebook, said the earthquake occurred at 6.6 degrees North and 118.3 degrees East.
The epicentre was located 354km south of Palawan, Philippines, and at a depth of 392km.
MetMalaysia said the earthquake posed no tsunami threat to Malaysia.
