Title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for northern states, Sabah and Sarawak until noon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning covering multiple states across the country, cautioning that thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected until 12 noon today.
In the northern peninsula, the entire state of Perlis is under warning, along with several districts in Kedah, including Bandar Baharu, Kulim, Pendang, Pokok Sena, Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Kuala Muda, Yan and Baling.
Penang is also affected in its entirety, while Perak faces widespread impact across Hulu Perak, Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Perak Tengah and Kuala Kangsar.
Further south, the whole of Melaka has been placed under the warning, alongside three districts in Johor — Muar, Tangkak and Batu Pahat.
In East Malaysia, Sarawak's Miri division is expected to see stormy conditions across Marudi, Beluru, Miri and Subis, with Limbang also included.
Sabah faces the broadest exposure in the region, with the Interior areas of Kuala Penyu, Beaufort, Membakut and Sipitang under warning, as well as the West Coast districts of Papar, Kota Belud, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Putatan and Penampang. W.P. Labuan rounds out the list of affected areas.
MetMalaysia explained that a thunderstorm warning is triggered when signs point to storms bringing rainfall exceeding 20mm per hour, either imminent or expected to persist for more than an hour.
Such warnings are valid for no longer than six hours per issuance.
Residents and motorists in the affected areas have been urged to exercise caution, particularly given the risk of flash floods and reduced visibility associated with heavy downpours and strong winds.

Title: Weak 3.7-magnitude earthquake strikes off Sandakan, no tsunami threat to Malaysia
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 18 — A weak earthquake measuring 3.7 on the Richter scale was detected about 88 kilometres north of Sandakan, Sabah at 10.30pm yesterday.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement on Facebook, said the earthquake occurred at coordinates 6.6 degrees North and 118.3 degrees East.
It said the epicentre was about 354 kilometres south of Palawan, Philippines and 88 kilometres north of Sandakan, at a depth of 392 kilometres.
MetMalaysia said the earthquake posed no tsunami threat to Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Passenger dies after medical emergency on Malaysia Airlines flight to Sydney
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A passenger died on board a Sydney-bound Malaysia Airlines flight after suffering a critical medical emergency mid-air on Wednesday.
Malaysia Airlines confirmed that the passenger on board flight MH141 from Kuala Lumpur to Sydney could not be revived despite immediate emergency medical intervention by crew members and qualified medical personnel on board,
news.com.au
reported.
A doctor, three nurses, and a cabin crew member rushed to assist the passenger and administered cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), but the doctor on board subsequently pronounced the individual dead.
The passenger, who was travelling alongside a family member, was identified by
Daily Mail Australia
as a 58-year-old Indian national who suffered a severe asthma attack during the eight-hour journey.
The flight departed Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday morning and touched down at Sydney Airport at 7.43pm local time.
New South Wales Police confirmed that officers were alerted at the international terminal around 5.50pm regarding a medical emergency involving a 58-year-old man on an inbound flight from Malaysia.
Authorities said the death is not being treated as suspicious and no further police investigation is expected.
In a statement yesterday, Malaysia Airlines extended its sincere condolences to the passenger’s family and apologised to travellers affected by delays and disruptions to flights MH141 and its return service, MH140.

Title: Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s Office backs AGC view, says won’t gazette April 19 proclamation on Ruler
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 18 — The Negeri Sembilan government will not take any action to gazette or enforce the April 19, 2026 proclamation regarding the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar, the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s (SUK) office said in a statement last night.
It said the decision aligned with the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) ruling that the proclamation was invalid, rendering any gazettement unconstitutional.
It said the state government abided by the AGC’s view that members of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (MMKN) had no jurisdiction, authority, or power under the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 to announce the proclamation.
“Furthermore, there is no legal basis for MMKN members to rely on the proclamation dated April 19, 2026 for their announcement,” it said.
The SUK office was referring to statements made by Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to the media yesterday regarding instructions to gazette the proclamation as decided by the MMKN.
“In this regard, the state administration has referred the matter to the State Legal Adviser to ensure that any necessary action is carried out in accordance with current laws and the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959,” the office added.
The AGC in a statement last night said the proclamation dated April 19 regarding the position of Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, was invalid as it failed to comply with mandatory requirements under Article 10 of the state constitution.
It also clarified that the Menteri Besar and the MMKN did not have unilateral authority to depose or declare vacant the office of the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Meanwhile, the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) reiterated that Tuanku Muhriz remained the legitimate Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and chairman of the DKU. — Bernama

Title: FT Pardons Board convenes at Istana Negara amid talk of Najib’s petition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh and Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar have both reached Istana Negara here for a suddenly-scheduled Pardons Board meeting this morning.
Yeoh’s convoy was seen entering the palace gates at 7.48am, followed closely by a vehicle carrying Mohd Dusuki,
NST
reported.
Both sit as statutory members on the board, which is chaired by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
The meeting is shrouded by speculation that the board is being reconvened to determined pardon application of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which had been deferred during the previous meeting on Sept 11.
At the time, Najib had been expected to receive some form of pardon.
Last night, Yeoh had dismissed a viral document circulating on social media regarding Najib’s purported house arrest, clarifying that her signature did not appear on the paper.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
In 2024, the FT Pardons Board halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
However, Najib and his lawyers subsequently insisted that the partial pardon came with a royal addendum for him to serve out his remaining time at home, eventually suing to have this granted.
On Dec 22 last year, the High Court dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib withdrew his appeal against the decision in April this year.

Title: New-generation MyKad drops Touch ’n Go feature, focuses on security, says NRD
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The new-generation MyKad, which started being issued yesterday, no longer comes with the Touch ’n Go facility.
In a social media post, the National Registration Department (NRD) said users can still access the service through the Touch ’n Go eWallet or a separate Touch ’n Go card.
“For users who wish to continue using Touch ’n Go services, the facility can be accessed through the Touch ’n Go eWallet or a separate Touch ’n Go card,” it said.
According to NRD, the new-generation MyKad focuses on its primary function as the country’s official identity document, while incorporating enhanced security and technological features.
Equipped with 53 security features, the new-generation MyKad includes enhanced security elements such as a Dynamic Security Hologram and a transparent window on the front, as well as an Enforcement QR Code and a Dual-Function Interface Chip on the back.
The new MyKad is also expected to have enhanced identity verification capabilities while reducing the risk of forgery and misuse of identity documents.
NRD said the transparent window feature strengthens protection against forgery, while the QR code supports verification and enforcement requirements.
Meanwhile, the Dynamic Security Hologram displays a three-dimensional image that changes according to the viewing angle and lighting, while the UV feature reveals specific security elements that are only visible under ultraviolet light.
Guilloche patterns and microtext have also been incorporated as additional security features, while the polycarbonate layer makes the MyKad more resistant to heat and chemicals, thereby enhancing the card’s durability.
Applications for the new-generation MyKad can be made at 40 NRD branches equipped with printing facilities, where the cards can be issued on the same day.
At NRD branches without printing facilities, applications for the new-generation MyKad can still be made, with the cards ready within five working days. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak and Selangor bear the brunt as 34 stations log ‘Unhealthy’ API levels in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Air quality across Malaysia deteriorated significantly this morning, with 34 monitoring stations nationwide recording “Unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels as of 8.30am, according to Department of Environment (DoE) data.
Readings across the country spanned between 104 and 198, indicating widespread haze coverage across both Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak.
Johan Setia in Selangor recorded the nation’s worst air quality at 198, hovering just two points shy of the 200 mark that triggers a “Very Unhealthy” classification.
The next four most severely affected locations were concentrated heavily in Sarawak and the central-southern peninsula: Kuching (192), Samarahan (184), Nilai in Negeri Sembilan (181), and IPD Serian (180).
Sarawak and Selangor hardest hit
Sarawak emerged as the most affected state overall, with eight monitoring stations entering the unhealthy range. Alongside Kuching, Samarahan, and Serian, elevated levels were registered in Sibu (158), Sarikei (157), Bintulu (153), Sri Aman (153), and Mukah (104).
Selangor recorded the highest concentration of polluted areas in Peninsular Malaysia, with six stations logging unhealthy air quality.
Beyond Johan Setia, elevated readings were recorded in Shah Alam (171), Banting (167), Petaling Jaya (162), Klang (161), and Kuala Selangor (148).
Central and southern regions
The haze sat heavily across the greater Klang Valley and neighboring southern states. In the Federal Territories, Putrajaya posted a reading of 173, while Kuala Lumpur logged 166 in Cheras and 164 in Batu Muda.
In Negeri Sembilan, Nilai led with 181, followed by Seremban at 171 and Port Dickson at 159. Melaka recorded three affected stations: Alor Gajah (165), Bukit Rambai (162), and Bandaraya Melaka (153).
Further south in Johor, five locations crossed into the unhealthy bracket, comprising Tangkak (159), Segamat (158), Batu Pahat (155), Kluang (152), and Larkin (128).
Perak and the east coast
In Perak, four stations registered unhealthy levels, led by Seri Manjung at 176 and Tasek Ipoh at 172, while Pegoh Ipoh and Tanjung Malim both tied at 152.
On the East Coast, Pahang recorded two affected stations, with Temerloh at 151 and Jerantut at 107.
The lowest readings among the 34 affected stations were recorded in Mukah (104) and Jerantut (107).
The DoE is continuing round-the-clock air quality surveillance, with conditions expected to fluctuate depending on prevailing wind directions and regional hotspot activity.

Title: Ice, fans and cooling pads: How Malaysia’s chicken farmers are beating El Niño heat
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 18 — Inside a closed-house chicken farm in Jalan Kebun here, Mohd Muzamri Shoib instructed one of his workers to open the door.
He chose the worker deliberately.
As the door opened, Muzamri watched the flock before explaining why even a simple interruption to their routine could cause stress.
“These chickens can get stressed when someone they do not recognise opens the door,” he said.
But an unfamiliar presence is not the only source of stress for the birds.
Heat poses a far more serious challenge, and one that farmers cannot simply keep outside the door.
A prolonged spell of extreme heat could affect how quickly chickens grow, how much farmers lose and how well they perform.
Keeping the heat out
Malay Mail
recently visited Muzamri’s farm, where the broiler farmer and chairman of the Selangor Poultry Farmers Association has spent 26 years raising chickens.
With a very strong El Niño expected to develop towards the end of this year, Malaysia could face extreme heat and dry weather from January to May 2027, with temperatures potentially reaching 40°C, according to MetMalaysia.
Farmers like Muzamri are therefore relying on systems that have become an increasingly important part of modern poultry farming.
His farm has two closed-house poultry buildings, one with two levels and another with a single level, both equipped with cooling pads and exhaust fans designed to keep temperatures under control.
The cooling pads line the walls of the buildings, with water pumped from large tanks and circulated through them before air is drawn through and cooled.
Muzamri inside his closed-house chicken farm in Jalan Kebun, Shah Alam. — Picture by Yusof Isa
At the other end, large exhaust fans pull the air out while helping to remove ammonia and odours from the building.
The result is a controlled environment in which the temperature can be adjusted according to the age of the chickens.
Younger birds, for instance, require warmer conditions, with temperatures of around 37°C being more comfortable for them, similar to the warmth they would experience with a mother hen.
For older broilers, however, excessive heat becomes a growing concern.
When chickens start to overheat
Professor Datuk Zulkifli Idrus, director of the Institute of Tropical Agriculture and Food Security at Universiti Putra Malaysia, said chickens were particularly vulnerable to prolonged heat because they could not sweat like humans.
Their bodies are covered with feathers, making it harder for them to lose heat.
Instead, chickens mainly cool themselves by panting and increasing blood flow to their skin, combs and wattles.
“When temperatures remain high, they pant more, become less active, eat less and drink more,” he said.
If the heat continues, the birds can become dehydrated and their normal bodily functions can be disrupted.
Severe and prolonged heat stress can eventually result in organ failure and death, Zulkifli said.
For broiler farmers, the problem is compounded by the birds’ rapid growth.
Modern broilers become heavy quickly and generate considerable body heat, making birds approaching market weight particularly vulnerable when temperatures rise.
Broiler chickens at Muzamri’s closed-house chicken farm. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Cooling the flock
Muzamri said his farm’s environmental control system allows him to regulate the temperature, ventilation and feeding of the chickens.
The system is currently operated through controls at the farm, although he is looking to upgrade it so the same functions can be managed through a smartphone.
That would allow him to monitor and adjust the system even when he is away from the farm.
The controls can be used for the chicken feeders, cooling pads and fans.
And when the heat becomes particularly intense, Muzamri has another measure ready.
He buys bags of ice and puts them into a reservoir through which water passes before being pumped towards the cooling pads.
He normally orders about 30 large bags, which he said can last five to six days.
The farm has about eight water tanks, roughly the size of those commonly found in the attics of Malaysian landed homes.
Heat stress on chickens
For Muzamri, these preparations are not new.
The system has been in use for years, but the prospect of a prolonged period of extreme heat means there is little room for complacency.
“My farming activities are primarily focused on broiler chickens, but hot weather and maintaining temperatures in poultry houses are indeed very important issues for the poultry industry as a whole, particularly the broiler sector.
“When excessively hot weather occurs, chickens can experience heat stress. The effects depend on the type and age of the chickens.
“For broilers, some of the common concerns include reduced feed intake, slower growth, poorer feed conversion ratio and an increased risk of mortality if temperature and ventilation are not properly controlled,” he said.
Professor Datuk Zulkifli Idrus, director of the Institute of Tropical Agriculture and Food Security at Universiti Putra Malaysia, said chickens were particularly vulnerable to prolonged heat because they could not sweat like humans. — Picture by Yusof Isa
These systems are increasingly important for modern farmers, particularly those operating closed-house farms, where exhaust fans, cooling pads, tunnel ventilation systems, temperature and humidity sensors and automatic controllers are used to manage heat.
“When temperatures rise, these systems increase ventilation and use cooling pads to help lower the temperature inside the poultry house,” Muzamri said.
“We also incur costs to purchase ice to help cool the poultry houses during the hottest part of the day, between 11am and 3pm.”
But keeping chickens cool is not simply a matter of turning on more fans.
Water is just as important.
Zulkifli said chickens drink substantially more during hot weather as they try to replace fluids lost through panting and cool their bodies.
A constant supply of clean drinking water that is not excessively warm is therefore essential, while farmers must also ensure their generators and emergency power supplies are working.
A power failure during extreme heat can be particularly dangerous in a closed-house system because the ventilation and cooling systems can stop at the moment they are most needed.
Muzamri said his preparations also extend to giving the chickens drinks containing rock sugar and other supplements intended to help them cope with the heat.
“We also provide chickens with drinks that can help cool their bodies, including rock sugar and other additional supplements, to help regulate their body temperature,” he said.
For open-house farms, where conditions inside the poultry houses are more directly affected by the weather outside, farmers must pay closer attention to ventilation, fans, shading, water supply and stocking density.
Preparing for prolonged heat
Zulkifli said the greatest risk was not necessarily a single exceptionally hot afternoon, but a prolonged spell in which high temperatures persisted day after day, particularly when nights remained warm and gave the birds little opportunity to recover.
“The problem is not just one unusually hot afternoon, but a series of hot days over a long period, especially if the night temperatures stay high and the birds have little time to recover,” he said.
The combination of temperature, humidity, ventilation and water availability determines how severe the heat stress becomes.
Adult chickens generally begin to experience heat stress when temperatures rise above about 26°C, particularly when humidity is high, he said.
The risk becomes considerably greater once temperatures reach 32°C to 35°C and above.
High humidity makes panting less effective because the birds struggle to release heat through evaporation.
For broilers, the consequences can extend beyond animal welfare and into production.
Heat-stressed birds eat less, grow more slowly and can become less efficient at converting feed into body weight.
Severe or prolonged heat stress can also increase mortality.
Modern broilers become heavy quickly and generate considerable body heat, making birds approaching market weight particularly vulnerable when temperatures rise. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Laying hens face a different set of problems.
Reduced feed intake means fewer nutrients and less energy are available for egg production, while prolonged heat exposure can interfere with reproductive processes.
The result can be fewer and smaller eggs, as well as poorer eggshell quality.
For farmers, the priority is therefore to prevent heat stress before it becomes severe.
“Fans, cooling pads, water pumps, sensors, generators and water supplies need to be inspected and maintained more frequently,” Muzamri said.
At Muzamri’s farm, much of that infrastructure is already in place.
The technology may eventually move further away from the farm floor and into the farmer’s hand, with smartphone controls allowing Muzamri to monitor conditions and operate equipment remotely.
For now, however, the principle remains the same as it has throughout his 26 years in the industry: keep the birds comfortable, keep the air moving and make sure there is enough water.
With the heat expected to intensify, those preparations could become increasingly important.

Title: AGC: Exco statement has no legal effect, move to gazette or implement proclamation on N. Sembilan Yamtuan’s removal invalid, unconstitutional
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) said the Negeri Sembilan state executive council’s media statement or announcement has no legal effect as its members had no jurisdiction, authority or power under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959 to make it.
The AGC said there was also no legal basis for the state executive council members to rely on the April 19, 2026 proclamation for their announcement, adding that any move to gazette or implement the proclamation would be invalid and unconstitutional.
In a statement today, the AGC said it had taken note of the document titled “Media Statement of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council — Decision of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council Meeting No. 6 of 2026 (September 15, 2026)”.
It said the Menteri Besar and state executive council did not have unilateral power to terminate or declare vacant the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, while the validity and effect of the proclamation must be determined through a valid constitutional and legal process, particularly under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959.
The AGC said it had previously given the preliminary view that the April 19 proclamation was invalid because it did not comply with the mandatory requirements under Article 10 of the state constitution, particularly as there was no evidence that any of the disqualifying factors under Article 10(1) applied to Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
It said although the Datuk-Datuk Undang have the power to take action to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Article 10 also provides the procedures and grounds for consideration before such a decision can be made.
“To date, there are no facts indicating that the prescribed procedures have been complied with,” it said.
The AGC also said an issue had arisen over whether some of the Datuk-Datuk Undang who signed the proclamation were lawfully holding office, as they had been removed according to the customary practices of their respective luak.
“The validity of several Undang who signed the proclamation is disputed because their removal was carried out according to the customs of their respective luak,” it said.
“Therefore, the composition of the Undang Yang Empat was in fact incomplete at the material time,” it added.
The AGC said it respected the position of the Datuk-Datuk Undang and acknowledged that the appointment and removal of each of them were subject to the customary rules of their respective luak.
It said the 1959 state constitution also provides for the establishment of the Dewan Undangan dan Keadilan, with Article 16 placing matters concerning Malay customs, including the selection, appointment, placement and removal of Undang, as well as matters brought by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, under the Dewan’s jurisdiction.
Under Article 16(3), it said, the Dewan’s advice on such matters is final and cannot be challenged or questioned in any court on any grounds.
The AGC also said the matter was currently before the High Court of Malaya in Seremban and that an interlocutory injunction remained in force.
It urged all parties to respect the court process and allow the matter to be resolved in an orderly manner.

Title: Second body recovered as search continues for missing Pulau Ketam anglers
Article:
KLANG, Sept 17 — Another body, believed to be one of the anglers missing off One Fathom Bank near Pulau Ketam on Sunday, was found floating off Hutan Melintang, Perak, late this afternoon.
Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) operations officer, Maritime Lieutenant Mohd Syafiq Sazali said a local fishing boat spotted a man’s body floating at 4.26 pm.
“The discovery was immediately relayed to Perak MMEA for further action.
“The MMEA vessel KM Nusa, conducting search operations in the area, proceeded to the location about three nautical miles from the Selangor–Perak maritime boundary,” he told reporters at the Search and Rescue (SAR) Forward Operating Base at the Sementa Jetty here today.
Mohd Syafiq added that the latest recovery was about two nautical miles from where the first victim, Mohd Shahril Abd Rahman, was found yesterday.
“The body, wearing a life jacket, will be brought ashore at the Hutan Melintang Jetty. Police will handle formal identification with family members or next of kin,” he said.
Meanwhile, the family of missing angler Muhammad Ridzuan Ruhaizat, 37, remains hopeful he will be found safe.
The victim’s uncle, Khairul Muhidin, 47, said he last met his nephew, a contractor with a utility company, at his Jalan Kebun residence on September 4, where they mostly chatted about work.
“On the night of the incident (Sunday), I was shocked when family members informed me. I immediately dialled the 999 emergency line,” he told reporters at the Sementa Jetty.
Khairul said the family is hopeful Muhammad Ridzuan is safe. He described his nephew, the fourth of six siblings and an avid angler, as resilient, noting he was wearing a life jacket during the incident.
“He might have held onto something or a container to stay afloat. Our main concern is dehydration at sea,” he said.
Khairul said two other relatives who survived the incident, namely Mohd Rizal Mohamad Sadali and Muhd Hamiszar Punirain, both 45, are reported to be in stable condition.
“Mohd Rizal was transferred to a private hospital in Shah Alam, while Muhd Hamiszar, who suffered neck injuries, is being treated at Hospital Banting. Both are stable but remain traumatised by the ordeal,” he said.
Earlier, Selangor Menteri Besar’s Political secretary Saifuddin Shafi Muhammad, visited the victim’s family and received a briefing on the latest developments of the incident.
Besides Mohd Rizal and Muhd Hamiszar, the other survivors were Mohd Shairazi Abdul Aziz, 43, and boat skipper Zulfikalnain Awang, 47. The four were rescued on the second day of the SAR.
The two remaining missing victims are Muhammad Ridzuan and Raja Mohd Rozi Raja Mohamad, 49. — Bernama

Title: KL to add 49ha of green spaces as city moves to protect open areas, says Hannah Yeoh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will create nearly 49 hectares of new recreational spaces and public parks across the capital, as part of efforts to expand the city’s network of green areas and recreational facilities.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the strategic initiative included pre-development works and the utilisation of Department of Irrigation and Drainage reserves along Sungai Bunus and Kolam Ayer Panas.
She said the development will also cover the pond area next to Jalan Tasik Permaisuri 3, as well as a phased project at the Kampung Sungai Bohol Retention Pond.
“Our main aim under this initiative is not merely to create new recreational spaces, but to ensure that every valuable open and green space in Kuala Lumpur is legally gazetted and protected,” she said after inspecting the Bunus Flood Retention Pond here today.
She said the areas will be equipped with basic infrastructure suitable for people of all ages, particularly senior citizens and children, such as jogging tracks and lighting, while enforcement will be tightened to prevent encroachment or unauthorised commercial activities.
Hannah said that through the continued efforts of the Federal Territories Land and Mines Office (PPTGWP), 556 open-space lots have now been gazetted, while more than 200 others are in the final stages of the gazettement process.
She said the transparency of the gazettement process allows city residents to check the list of protected open spaces themselves through the MyHijau application on the official PPTGWP portal.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said DBKL allocates more than RM200 million under Budget 2027 for the green cluster, covering the management, preservation and upgrading of public facilities.
He said DBKL submitted an application to the Ministry of Finance under a matching grant scheme to upgrade 14 neighbourhood children’s playgrounds to safer, more modern designs. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian woman, 40, dies during scuba dive in Bali’s Crystal Bay
Article:
BALI, Sept 17 — A 40-year-old Malaysian woman died while scuba diving in the waters off Crystal Bay, Desa Sakti, Bali, Indonesia, yesterday.
The victim, Siti Nuraini Rusidi, was reported to have died at about 11.10am local time, according to a report by
Sinar Harian
today.
According to local media portal BaliNews, Siti Nuraini joined a diving trip with a dive guide, boat captain and several other divers at about 8am.
However, concerns arose over her condition when the dive guide, Eugenius Franciso Ray, 33, noticed her coughing after they arrived at their first dive site at Manta Bay.
The dive guide reportedly asked about her condition, but Siti Nuraini said she was still able to continue with the activity until the dive at Manta Bay was completed.
The situation became tense after the group arrived at Crystal Bay, where they encountered very strong sea currents.
The conditions swept three divers away, while Siti Nuraini was reported to have died in the incident.
The incident later drew attention in Malaysia after a user shared details of the incident on Threads.

Title: Malaysia offers Indonesia aircraft, helicopters to fight forest fires amid haze concerns, says Zahid
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 17 — Malaysia has officially offered assistance to Indonesia in tackling forest fires, including a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft previously deployed to help its neighbour combat similar fires.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said this was conveyed to Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka during a meeting held in conjunction with his four-day working visit to the country, which began today.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the assistance would also include three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).
“The matter will be referred to President Prabowo Subianto for the Indonesian government’s approval,” he told a press conference after a memorandum of understanding (MoU) signing ceremony between the  Rural and Regional Development Ministry and Indonesia’s Ministry of Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions here today.
The visit, which runs until September 20, is at the invitation of Indonesia’s Halal Product Assurance Organising Agency (BPJPH) in conjunction with the 5th Halal 20 (H20) Summit.
Ahmad Zahid is scheduled to attend the opening ceremony tomorrow and participate as a panellist in a session on regional halal cooperation.
The MMEA’s Bombardier CL-415MP, which is capable of carrying out aerial firefighting operations, was previously deployed to South Sumatra in 2015, where it dropped 546,000 litres of water during a five-day mission.
Ahmad Zahid said the aircraft would draw water from lakes, seas or rivers before dropping it over fire-affected areas, while the three helicopters offered would also be deployed for the same purpose.
“Malaysia is deeply concerned about this problem, which occurs every year, whether due to open burning in Kalimantan or Sumatra, with the resulting haze reaching Malaysia.
“We want to help Indonesia address the problem together,” he said.
He said the assistance was not intended to interfere in Indonesia’s affairs, but rather to help address transboundary haze, which also affects neighbouring countries.
“What is important to us is to resolve this problem before it happens every year. This means having a mitigation plan or a strategy to prevent it from happening. The mitigation plan is in the interests of both Malaysia and Indonesia,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid said Malaysia and Indonesia also maintained close cooperation in disaster management through meetings and joint exercises, including at the Asean level. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Malaysian households using up to 800kWh exempt from AFA, Retail Charge and SST on electricity bills until Dec 31 amid haze, heat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The government has expanded electricity bill protection for domestic users from 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh) to 800kWh a month from September to December 31, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said in a Facebook post today.
He said the measure was an immediate step to ease the cost-of-living pressures faced by households, particularly as haze and hotter weather have driven up electricity consumption in some homes.
Under the expanded protection, domestic users consuming up to 800kWh a month will be exempted from the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), Retail Charge and Sales and Service Tax (SST).
Anwar also expressed his appreciation to Tenaga Nasional Bhd, the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry (Petra) and the Energy Commission for enabling the measure to be implemented quickly.
He said the recent haze and warmer weather had contributed to increased electricity consumption among some households, causing their monthly usage to exceed 600kWh and resulting in unusually higher bills.
“The Madani Government will continue to closely monitor developments in fuel costs and current energy market conditions to ensure that any decisions related to electricity tariffs take into account the balance between affordability and the people’s cost of living, electricity supply security and the sustainability of the national energy sector,” he said.

Title: Police probe Simpang Pulai road rage after Mercedes driver allegedly threatened with stick
Article:
IPOH, Sept 17 — Police are investigating an incident where a car driver was allegedly threatened with a wooden stick on Jalan Ipoh-Gopeng, Simpang Pulai, near here, yesterday.
The incident has now gone viral on the social media platform Threads.
Ipoh district police chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said today that the incident occurred at 4.56pm when the victim, driving a Mercedes, claimed that his vehicle was forced to the side by a Toyota Vios before a misunderstanding arose after the victim honked at the other vehicle.
“One of the two men who got out of the Toyota Vios was accused of carrying and pointing a stick at the victim’s brother. The incident was also recorded by a dashboard camera (dashcam), he said.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 506 of the Penal Code and efforts to track down the individuals involved are underway.
Therefore, he advised all road users to drive carefully, always control their emotions, and not act aggressively when facing any misunderstandings on the road. — Bernama

Title: Ipoh woman loses RM41,215 in online job and fake investment scams
Article:
IPOH, Sept 17 — A 36-year-old woman lost RM41,215 after falling victim to an online job scam and a non-existent investment scheme recently.
Muallim district police chief Supt Khalid Mohamad said the victim received a job offer through WhatsApp on September 13, with rewards offered for completing product evaluation tasks on the Shopee platform.
He said the victim was subsequently instructed to make several money transfers to bank accounts provided by the suspect.
“On September 15, the victim made six transactions totalling RM41,215 before being asked to make an additional payment of RM32,800. The victim realised that she had likely been scammed and did not proceed with the payment,” he said in a statement today.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: ‘Stare’ case at Kepong restaurant: AGC reviewing technician’s representation over grievous hurt charge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) is still reviewing a representation by a technician seeking reconsideration of a charge of causing grievous hurt to a man in a “stare” incident at a restaurant in Kepong here in May.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Adiba Iman Hassan said the representation by second accused Lai Kae Bin was submitted on September 2 and is still under consideration.
“The prosecution seeks to have it recorded that documents related to the case have been handed over to the defence,” she said during the case mention before Sessions Court Judge Noor Aini Yusof here today.
On May 14, Lai, 33, carpenter Wong Weng Luen, 49, and memorial centre worker Wan Ken Fei, 30, pleaded not guilty to intentionally causing grievous hurt to Andrew Teh Tiek Hua, 49, at a restaurant in Jalan Kepong, Metro Prima, at 2am on May 7.
The charge under Section 326 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same law, carries a maximum jail term of 20 years, and the offender may also be fined or caned upon conviction.
Adiba Iman said the prosecution was still awaiting Wong’s psychiatric assessment report, as well as a forensic report on closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and full medical reports from private and government hospitals concerning the complainant.
Wong was not brought to court today as he is undergoing psychiatric assessment at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak.
The court then fixed October 13 for the next case mention for the psychiatric report and submission of additional documents to the defence.
Lawyer Muhamad Firdaus Jumaludin, who represents Lai and Wong, told reporters after the proceedings that the representation was submitted seeking reconsideration of the Section 326 charge on the grounds that it was too serious.
“We (the defence) have examined the evidence in the case and do not see any intention on the part of (the second accused) to commit the act, as it happened spontaneously,” he said.
Lawyer Mohammad Arifin Abdul Wahab, who represents Wan, was also present during today’s proceedings.
Previously, a CCTV recording went viral on social media showing three individuals attacking a man, leaving him injured, after he was allegedly accused of staring at a group of people while they were eating at a restaurant in Kepong. — Bernama

Title: IGP: Police DNA lab logs 420 matches, seeks more technology for forensic investigations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The enhancement of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) DNA Analysis Laboratory through a RM11.1 million allocation under the 12th Malaysia Plan (12MP) has enabled PDRM to carry out 420 Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) matching cases, including those involving serious crimes.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, however, said PDRM still required additional logistics, equipment and technology to further strengthen its investigative capabilities and help solve more cases that require forensic analysis.
“The use of this technology helps PDRM trace various leads, especially evidence linked to a case, thereby strengthening the investigation process,” he told reporters after officiating the 7th National Forensic Science Symposium for Law Enforcement (NAFSLE) 2026 here today.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar and National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim were also present.
Mohd Khalid said other departments and agencies needing forensic analysis assistance could also use the PDRM Forensic Laboratory’s expertise, adding that the increased allocation would enable the adoption of more new technologies in the future.
Earlier, in his speech, he said the record 420 DNA matches reflected the success of forensic investigations conducted by forensic officers using high-technology equipment and artificial intelligence (AI) applications, which helped victims’ families get justice.
He said the government had also noted the backlog of 297,085 samples at the PDRM DNA Analysis Laboratory from 2021 to 2025, which has been one of the main challenges in expediting evidence analysis.
“As such, the government has created flexible positions for analysts at the PDRM DNA Analysis Laboratory as a strategic measure to enhance the efficiency of biological material analysis, while ensuring that the process complies with international standards,” he said.
Commenting on this year’s symposium themed “Forensic AI: Connecting the Dots”, Mohd Khalid urged PDRM personnel to make a paradigm shift by viewing AI as a strategic ally in forensic investigations, and not merely as an assistance tool.
“AI has the potential to speed up data analysis and improve accuracy in identifying links between cases, individuals and crime scenes, but its use remains subject to stipulated procedures and integrity,” he added.
The two-day symposium brought together over 300 participants, featuring eight invited speakers from various agencies and academic institutions, as well as exhibitions by local and overseas suppliers of technology and scientific equipment.
At the same event, three recipients of the Forensic DNA Databank Malaysia (FDDM) Hits of the Year Award were also announced for their success in obtaining DNA matches that assisted investigations into criminal cases in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Perak. — Bernama

Title: No evidence of established piranha population in Pahang’s Klau Dam yet, says Fisheries Dept
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Department of Fisheries (DOF) said today there is no evidence yet of an established or breeding piranha population in the Klau Dam, Raub, following the catch of a fish suspected to be of the species on August 26.
Fisheries director-general Datuk Adnan Hussain said only one such fish had so far been reported caught in the area, while investigations and field monitoring by the Pahang Fisheries Department up to September 15 found no additional catches or related safety incidents.
“Based on the technical assessment by the Fisheries Research Institute (FRI) in Glami Lemi, Negeri Sembilan, of photographs and video recordings of the fish, its observable morphological characteristics are consistent with the genus Pygocentrus, which is the piranha group.
“However, definitive confirmation at species level cannot be made as the physical specimen was not available for further examination. The fish was reported to have died and been disposed of by the individual who caught it before the investigation was conducted,” he said in a statement today.
Previously, social media was abuzz with claims of piranhas in the Klau Dam, including posts alleging that the fish had eaten a crocodile, raising concern among netizens over the possible presence of the alien species in the waters.
Adnan reminded the public not to panic, saying the DOF would continue regular monitoring at the Klau Dam and surrounding areas to identify any new developments, while increasing public awareness of the risks of releasing alien or invasive fish species into public waters.
He also said that releasing alien fish species that could become invasive into public waters was irresponsible as it could adversely affect inland aquatic ecosystems, local fish populations and aquatic biodiversity.
“If a fish suspected to be an alien species such as this is caught, do not release it back into the water. Keep the specimen if it is still in suitable condition and immediately contact the nearest fisheries office for further examination and analysis, including deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing if required,” he said.
The public is advised to obtain information from official DOF sources and avoid spreading unverified information to prevent confusion and speculation. — Bernama

Title: Haze: 30 areas across Malaysia record unhealthy air quality, including Ipoh, PJ, Shah Alam and Kuching
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — A total of 30 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today.
According to the Malaysia Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Tasek Ipoh in Perak recorded the highest reading at 188, while three other areas in the state also had unhealthy API readings, namely Seri Manjung (179), Pegoh Ipoh (158) and Taiping (155).
In Sarawak, three areas recorded unhealthy readings: Kuching (172), Serian IPD (172) and Samarahan (167).
In Selangor, the areas with unhealthy API readings were Johan Setia (164), Shah Alam (156), Banting (154), Petaling Jaya (152) and Klang (140), while Kedah had one area, namely Sungai Petani (155).
In the capital, similar readings were recorded in Cheras (155) and Batu Muda (151), while Putrajaya recorded an API reading of 158.
The affected areas in Melaka were Bukit Rambai (154), Alor Gajah (153) and Bandaraya Melaka (152), while in Johor there were four areas: Batu Pahat (155), Segamat (152), Tangkak (148) and Kluang (117).
Jerantut in Pahang recorded 154, while three areas in Penang were affected: Minden (153), Seberang Jaya (152) and Seberang Perai (151).
Other areas with unhealthy API readings were Nilai (158) and Seremban (155) in Negeri Sembilan, as well as Kuala Terengganu (151) in Terengganu.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 301 and above (hazardous). — Bernama

Title: Vodus study: Anwar records highest acceptance, first-choice support among PM hopefuls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has emerged as the strongest overall candidate for the prime ministership in a new national study by Vodus Research, recording the highest public acceptance, first-choice support and net acceptance among five prominent prospective candidates.
The Malaysia Prime Minister Candidate Study 2026 found that 46 per cent of respondents aware of the candidates said they would accept Anwar as prime minister, while 34 per cent named him as their first choice.
His net acceptance score stood at +19 percentage points, also the highest among the five candidates surveyed.
Anwar was also the most widely recognised figure in the study, with 93 per cent familiarity among respondents aware of the candidates.
His support was particularly strong in East Malaysia, where 41 per cent of respondents selected him as their top choice, compared with 28 per cent in Peninsular Malaysia.
Vodus Research founder Kelvin Goh said the findings showed that public assessments of potential national leaders went beyond a simple popularity contest, with familiarity, favourability, acceptability and first-choice support representing distinct measures.
“Anwar’s stronger support in East Malaysia may partly reflect his administration’s greater focus on Sabah and Sarawak, including progress on MA63-related matters, Sabah’s revenue entitlements, and Sarawak’s greater control over its resources,” he said in a statement.
“These moves have kept federal delivery, state rights, and fiscal fairness highly visible in the region, which may have strengthened perceptions of Anwar’s leadership there.”
Khairy Jamaluddin recorded 32 per cent acceptance and a net acceptance score of +15 percentage points, while Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi registered 17 per cent acceptance and +6 points.
Terengganu Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar recorded 13 per cent acceptance, while Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli had 17 per cent acceptance and a net acceptance score of -3 points.
The study also found that Anwar’s first-choice support was more than twice that of Khairy, who recorded 14 per cent, while Onn Hafiz and Rafizi each registered eight per cent and Samsuri six per cent.
On personal favourability, however, Khairy recorded the highest net favourability score at +51 points, followed by Samsuri at +44, Onn Hafiz at +43, Anwar at +39 and Rafizi at +32.
Among those who viewed Anwar favourably, respondents most often cited his ability to grow the economy and create opportunities, as well as his experience in leading Malaysia, handling foreign affairs, attracting foreign investment and governance.
Across the study, economic growth and opportunities, a clear vision for Malaysia, strong and capable leadership, and improving Malaysians’ living standards were among the recurring factors respondents associated with favourable views of political figures.
The study involved 1,482 Malaysian adults aged 18 and above nationwide, with fieldwork conducted from Aug 18 to Sept 1.
Vodus said the findings represented a snapshot of public views during the fieldwork period and were not an electoral forecast or endorsement of any candidate or political party.

Title: Army steps up drone surveillance on border routes amid unrest in southern Thailand
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 17 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) is using advanced drone technology to strengthen security monitoring in hard-to-reach areas along the Malaysia-Thailand border, particularly in response to the unrest in southern Thailand.
Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the technology enabled TDM to overcome the challenges posed by hilly and densely forested terrain, where physical patrols by troops were difficult.
“It is true that the border stretches over a long distance, and there are areas that cannot be patrolled due to the terrain.
“So, the aerial assets are used to gather information and provide a real-time overview before ground units are deployed to take further action,” he told Bernama at Terendak Camp, Sungai Udang here today.
Azhan also gave an assurance that border security remained tight, with round-the-clock operations in place.
“We do not deny that the terrain provides opportunities for illegal routes, but the situation remains under control. We will ensure that no elements are able to breach our border. There will be no compromise.
“Our personnel are provided with clear rules of engagement, under which firm and decisive action will be taken immediately,” he added.
Meanwhile, Azhan said his recent official visit to Russia, at the invitation of the Russian Ground Forces, was aimed at strengthening bilateral military ties.
“The main areas discussed with our Russian counterparts included training cooperation and opportunities for course exchanges, particularly in combined arms and artillery.
“Both sides are now in the final stages of finalising the arrangements before TDM personnel are sent to undergo the specialised training,” he said. — Bernama

Title: KLIA ranks first in Asia for connectivity in OAG Megahubs 2026 ranking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KUL) ranked fourth globally and first among all Asian airports in OAG’s Megahubs 2026 ranking, with connections to 154 destinations, while also topping the Low-Cost Carrier (LCC) Megahubs index with nearly 15,000 possible low-cost connections.
OAG, the intelligence partner for global travel, said its annual ranking of global airport connectivity showed Asia Pacific (APAC) dominating the index, with eight airports in the global top 20.
According to OAG in a statement, AirAsia operates 34 per cent of total flights at KUL, while Seoul Incheon ranked second in the LCC rankings with connectivity reaching 198 destinations.
The recovery of Chinese airports was another standout feature in APAC, with Shanghai Pudong rising from 19th to 14th globally, Guangzhou Baiyun International from 36th to 19th, and Hong Kong returning to the global top 20 at 20th. Tokyo Haneda also improved, rising from ninth to eighth globally.
“The Asia Pacific numbers tell two stories this year. The first is the completion of Chinese aviation's post-pandemic recovery; these airports are back in the top 20, and the data shows it.
“The second is how low-cost carriers have reshaped Southeast Asian connectivity, with 51 per cent of all seats in the region now operated by LCCs, well above the global average,” said OAG Head of APAC, Mayur Patel.
OAG added that Singapore Changi climbed significantly in the LCC rankings, from 10th to fifth, reflecting growth in destinations served and potential low-cost connections, while Fukuoka rose from 13th to eighth in the LCC index.
The average dominant carrier share at APAC’s top 10 airports is 33 per cent, lower than in most other regions, reflecting the diverse mix of full-service and low-cost carriers serving different traveller segments across Southeast and Northeast Asia. — Bernama

Title: Kota Kinabalu airport runway temporarily closed for rectification works
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 17 — The runway at Kota Kinabalu International Airport has been temporarily closed to facilitate rectification works, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said today.
In a notice on Facebook, MAHB said a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) had been issued over the temporary closure.
“The runway will reopen once the necessary safety inspections and clearing works have been completed,” it said.
Passengers have been advised to check with their respective airlines for the latest flight status and updates.
MAHB did not provide details on the nature of the rectification works or how long the runway would remain closed.

Title: Papagomo fails to stay RM280,000 defamation payout to Lim Guan Eng, son
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The High Court today dismissed an application by Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, to stay the execution of a judgment ordering him to pay RM280,000 in damages to former Penang Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng and his son.
Judge Roslan Mat Nor, in dismissing the application, ruled that the defendant had failed to establish any special circumstances warranting a stay of execution pending the disposal of his appeal, which was filed on June 2.
“The defendant claimed that he would succeed in his appeal and that the appeal would be rendered academic if the judgment sum was paid now. The defendant also contended that he would face bankruptcy proceedings if the plaintiffs executed the judgment.
“These reasons do not assist the court in exercising its discretion to grant a stay,” he said, and ordered Wan Muhammad Azri to pay RM5,000 in costs.
On May 19 this year, the court ruled that Wan Muhammad Azri was liable for defamation and ordered him to pay RM280,000 in damages to Guan Eng and Clint Lim Way Chau over the latter's posts alleging that Way Chau was detained in Singapore for purportedly bringing in RM2 million in undeclared cash in 2020.
The court ordered the defendant to pay global damages of RM200,000 and costs of RM30,000 to Guan Eng as well as damages of RM80,000 and costs of RM10,000 to the second plaintiff (Way Chau).
The duo filed the suit on April 19, 2020, alleging that the defendant had posted defamatory statements on his Facebook page claiming that Way Chau was detained at Changi Airport on February 29, 2020, for bringing in RM2 million in undeclared cash.
Guan Eng said the defendant, who uploaded the post under the name ‘Papa Azri’ on March 14, 2020, also claimed that Guan Eng had travelled to Singapore on February 29, 2020, after the alleged detention.
Lawyer Simon Murali attended today's proceedings, representing both plaintiffs, while lawyer Fazilah Jaafar represented Wan Muhammad Azri. — Bernama

Title: Palm oil mill shut down after pump failure sends effluent into Johor’s Sungai Sembrong
Article:
KLUANG, Sept 17 — A palm oil mill in Kluang has been identified as the source of pollution in Sungai Sembrong and ordered to halt operations immediately.
The directive was issued by the Kluang branch of the Department of Environment (DoE) following an investigation and inspection of the facility after pollution in the river was first detected on Monday.
“Further investigation revealed a pump malfunction at the mill’s effluent treatment pond, causing an overflow of oil-contaminated effluent into Sungai Sembrong.
“The mill has been ordered to halt operations immediately and is required to carry out cleanup and repair works. Follow-up action on the suspension of its licence is also underway,” the DoE said in a statement today.
Dead fish and prawns had previously been found along stretches of Sungai Sembrong, with the pollution reportedly affecting the livelihoods of nearby Orang Asli villagers.
The DoE reminded industries, particularly palm oil mill operators, to strictly comply with requirements under the Environmental Quality Act 1974 and the department’s licensing conditions.
It warned that stern action, including the suspension or revocation of licences, would be taken against any breach of the Act that causes environmental pollution or threatens drinking water supplies or public health.

Title: BPHB unit appointed Bintulu Port operator for 30 years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) has appointed Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd's (BPHB) wholly-owned subsidiary Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd (BPSB) as an approved port operator for Bintulu Port for 30 years, from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2056.
BPHB said the appointment was approved by the Sarawak legislative assembly.
“The appointment is set out in the Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) (Appointment of Approved Port Operator) Notification, 2026, published in the Sarawak Government Gazette, Part II, dated September 10, 2026. The notification was made under section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961,” it said in a stock exchange filing.
On June 23, 2026, the Sarawak Ministry of Infrastructure and Port Development notified BPSB that the government had approved in principle the appointment of BPSB as the approved port operator for Bintulu Port under Section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961.
BPHB said BPSB “shall perform, carry out or provide the port undertakings at Bintulu Port subject to full compliance with the ordinance and any by-laws, regulations or subsidiary legislation made under it.”
BPSB will also carry out the terms and conditions of the Heads of Agreement (HOA) dated July 27, 2026, entered into between the Sarawak state government, Bintulu Port Authority and BPSB, it added.
“The HOA terms and conditions shall continue to apply until the Port Operation Concession Agreement (POCA) is duly executed by those parties. Upon execution, the POCA shall be binding on BPSB and govern its operation of Bintulu Port,” said BPHB. — Bernama

Title: PMO says letter claiming Cabinet approval for PLUS highway widening is fake
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) today said that a letter dated July 17, 2026, claiming that Cabinet approval had been given for a proposed Private Finance Initiative (PFI) project to widen the North-South Expressway (PLUS) is fake.
In a statement today, PMO stressed that the Prime Minister had never issued or signed the letter and denied any connection with the document or the purported approval.
“PMO has lodged a police report over the forgery of the document and the misuse of the Prime Minister’s name and PMO’s official identity.
“Appropriate legal action will be taken against any party found to be involved,” the statement read.
PMO therefore advised the public not to be deceived by, circulate, or share the fake document. — Bernama

Title: Critics of Anwar should back their words with action, says PKR Youth chief
Article:
IPOH, Sept 17 — PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim has hit out at those criticising Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying some were quick to make political statements but lacked the courage to follow through with their actions.
He said while there were political statements suggesting that the country was currently unstable, the government remained committed to ensuring political stability as a foundation for economic stability and, ultimately, the benefit of the people.
“Our priority is to ensure political stability because from there, we can ensure economic stability, which will ultimately benefit the people,” he said.
He spoke to reporters after presenting allocations to non-governmental organisations in the Prime Minister’s Tambun parliamentary constituency at the Penghulu Mukim Hulu Kinta Office here.
Muhammad Kamil, who is also Anwar’s political secretary, said he did not deny that certain groups were deliberately attempting to create political instability to serve the interests and demands of certain leaders within their respective parties.
“Today, what we can assure the people is that the current government, particularly the Prime Minister, is committed to ensuring that all policies and plans can be implemented and that the government works for the good and benefit of the people as a whole,” he said.
He said this remained the case despite some statements appearing to attack Anwar personally.
“Some people are brave enough to talk, but they are not brave enough to act.
“So, we need to assess which leaders are working and which leaders are merely playing politics. I think the people can make a good assessment of that,” he said.
Muhammad Kamil also said there appeared to be confusion among the public when some political figures called for the 16th general election (GE16) to be held soon while at the same time saying they would remain in the government until the end of its term.
“That is something you have to ask that person. In the morning they say one thing, and at night they say another. They are confusing people,” he said.
Muhammad Kamil was responding to recent remarks made during the Umno general assembly, where party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi challenged Anwar to remove Umno from the unity government and face a confidence vote in Parliament.
Ahmad Zahid was also reported to have reminded coalition partners that Anwar’s administration remained in power with Umno’s support.
“The Prime Minister is the prime minister because of Umno’s support,” Ahmad Zahid was quoted as saying.
Ahmad Zahid was also reported to have backed calls for an earlier general election during the assembly.

Title: Melaka assembly dissolution date still undecided, says CM
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Sept 17 — The date for the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly to pave the way for the state election has yet to be set, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said several state administrative matters needed to be resolved first to ensure all plans proceeded smoothly before the assembly was dissolved.
“I am giving an indication that the Melaka State Assembly will be dissolved from Friday to Friday because within that period, we still have many matters that need to be resolved to govern the state,” he told reporters here today.
He was speaking after officiating the 2026 Melaka State-level Senior Citizens Day, Persons with Disabilities (PwD) Day and Children's Day celebration in conjunction with the Tanjung Bidara constituency's
Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat
(WRUR) programme here.
Ab Rauf said the date would be announced to the media and the public once it had been finalised.
On Tuesday, allegations went viral on WhatsApp claiming that Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam had signed the Melaka State Assembly dissolution document together with Ab Rauf during a meeting at the Guest Room of the Chief Executive Officer's Office at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh.
The Melaka State Assembly has 28 seats, while the current state government's mandate expires on December 31. — Bernama
